description:
FOUND + FIXED s470bw (2026-09-06), while reading the CPAN board's warm/cold
pair for #1261.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s470bw/lu-args.pl):
  perl: first nargs=0  any nargs=0  all nargs=0  none nargs=0  notall nargs=0
  PCL : first nargs=1  any nargs=1  all nargs=1  none nargs=1  notall nargs=1
`lib/List/Util.pm` called `$code->($_)` at those five sites.  perl's XS
MULTICALL (and its own pure-Perl fallback) sets `$_` and passes no arguments.

WHY IT MATTERS: invisible in the `{ BLOCK }` form (a block ignores @_), fatal
in the `\&NAME` form.  Scalar-List-Utils t/first.t:

    sub rec { my $n = shift;
              if (!defined($n)) { return 1 }        # perl reaches this
              if ($n < 5) { rec($n+1) }
              else { $v = first \&rec, 1,2 } }
    rec(1);

Under PCL `$n` was the ELEMENT (1), never undef, so `first \&rec` re-entered
rec(1) forever.  The run ended in an SBCL binding-stack exhaustion; the file
scored 12 of 24 rows (blessed board `PARTIAL 12 1`).  AFTER the fix it scores
23 of 24 â the residue is row 12 "undef active sub", which wants perl's
`Can't undef active subroutine` diagnostic (PCL emits none; the established
error-fidelity class).

HOW IT SURFACED, which is worth recording: #1261's runtime work flipped that
file from "SBCL prints the backtrace and exits (rc=1, 12 rows)" to "SBCL
re-exhausts the binding stack while printing the backtrace and LIVELOCKS
(rc=124, 0 rows)".  Bisected hunk by hunk against a `git archive 9ee95f2`
extraction (scratch/s470bw/bisect*.pl): the flip follows the compile-dirs
policy hunks even in a probe that never CALLS the new code, and 100 inert
defuns of the same size do NOT reproduce it â i.e. the trigger is an image
knife-edge in SBCL's disabled-debugger backtrace print, not a semantic
consequence.  The CAUSE, in both directions, is the infinite recursion, and
fixing it removes the knife-edge with it.  If a future change ever makes a
recursive-callback file livelock again, look for the recursion first.

The other five `$code->()` sites in the shim (reduce x2, pairfirst, pairgrep,
pairmap) were already argument-free.

SHIPPED as `7a2fcf1`; guard `Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t` 126 -> 127 rows, expectation
probed against perl.
subject: List::Util's block family called the block with the ELEMENT as an argument; perl sets $_ and passes NOTHING -- fatal for a `\&NAME` callback that does `my $n = shift` (Scalar-List-Utils t/first.t recursed forever)
